name: H5N1 bird flu
value: 3 cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Three Yakima County H5N1 cases linked to infected farm animals, one fatal; no human-to-human spread reported
state: Yakima County, Washington, reported two more human H5N1 cases on 31 Oct and 1 Nov, one of them fatal, making three in the county in 2026, all with exposure to infected animals on farms (UKHSA; CIDRAP). Close contacts are being monitored and CIDRAP reports no suggestion of human-to-human transmission. Washington recorded 34 infected dairy herds in the past 30 days (CIDRAP). Searches found no newer human case as of 9 Nov, so these remain animal-to-human cases.
for_you: Risk to the general public is described as low by US health officials. People who work with poultry or cattle are the most exposed; UKHSA and WHO publish guidance on avoiding contact with sick or dead animals.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only: three Yakima cases, all farm-exposed, no human-to-human spread reported (CIDRAP): Normal.
